tier_reason: First-party README benchmark against vanilla and tuned cublasXt with public benchmark code (examples/multiply.cpp, examples/cublasXt-multiply.cpp, examples/compare.sh) and GPU model plus CUDA 10.1 stated, but the compiler, flags and host CPU model of the run are not stated and the measured 2019 code was later fixed for wrong-result bugs, so it stays C. Not peer-reviewed.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README chart docs/performance.svg (tables of numbers rendered as an image): DGEMM time Tiled-MM vs cublasXt vanilla 83 vs 167 ms at n=4000 up to 16205 vs 76882 ms at n=32000 (2.0x to 4.7x, derived from page data); throughput 4044.18 vs 852.42 GFlop/s at n=32000 (89.87% vs 18.94% of 4500 GFlop/s peak). Against tuned cublasXt: 83 vs 127 ms at n=4000 (1.5x, derived), 352 vs 412 ms at n=8000 (1.17x, derived), and parity within about 1% from n=12000 to 32000 (tuned cublasXt slightly faster at 20000: 4252 vs 4282 ms, and 28000: 11113 vs 11171 ms).
corrections.hardware: One Piz Daint (Cray XC50) node with an NVIDIA P100 GPU (chart states peak 4500 GFlop/s, CUDA toolkit 10.1); host CPU model not stated
corrections.caveats: Numbers exist only inside the README's chart image (docs/performance.svg), not in text. The clear win is over vanilla cublasXt (2.0-4.7x); against a hand-tuned cublasXt (tile 4000, pinned memory) it is 1.5x at n=4000 and 1.17x at n=8000 and only on par from n=12000 upward. Compiler and flags for the run are not stated (README build example uses gcc-8; CMake defaults to Release); host CPU not stated. The chart sizes (4000-32000) do not match examples/compare.sh (4000-20000), so the exact run script is not published. Correctness bugs were fixed after the 2019 measurements ('Fixed the wrong results bug for certain tile sizes', Feb 2024; synchronization issue that 'would sometimes' return an incorrect result, Jun 2024). P100/CUDA 10.1-era data. Baseline cublasXt is not one of OpenBLAS, MKL, Eigen or BLIS.

notes: README text has no numbers, but the embedded performance.svg is a table of timings/throughputs plus a bar chart (rendered locally); the record understated the evidence. License BSD-3-Clause, 33 stars, not archived, not a fork, last commit 2024-12-06 (stale) all confirmed. Wrong-result bug fixes in 2024 are worth recording as a shortcoming.

tier_reason: Upgraded from C: the benchmark code is public (utils/time_kernel.cpp times the custom kernel against mkl_simatcopy with a result sanity check; build_and_run.sh -t -s runs the size sweep), the compiler is named in build_and_run.sh (clang-17/clang++-17), flags in CMakeLists.txt (-O3 -march=native -ffast-math, C++20, MKL 2025.1 sequential), and the CPU in the README (Intel i7-14700K @ 5.5 GHz).

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: '3-6x faster than MKL' (i7-14700K, Intel MKL 2025.1.0). Chart images/bandwidth_barchart_po2.png (values read approximately from the image): speedup about 1.4x at N=16, 2.7x at N=32, 3.1-3.3x at N=64-256, 4.9x at N=512, 4.4x at N=1024 and 6.2x at N=2048; custom kernel about 131-135 GB/s at N=64-512 vs MKL about 40-43 GB/s, falling to about 80 vs 13 GB/s at N=2048.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: clang-17 / clang++-17 (build_and_run.sh); -O3 -march=native -ffast-math, C++20 (CMakeLists.txt); MKL 2025.1 linked sequential (mkl_intel_lp64, mkl_sequential, mkl_core)
corrections.caveats: No LICENSE file (LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt, COPYING all 404; repo page shows none), so code cannot be copied. Numbers appear only in a chart image; the '3-6x' holds only for N>=64 (about 1.4x at N=16, 2.7x at N=32). The baseline call is mkl_simatcopy (in-place) on x86 and cblas_simatcopy from OpenBLAS on ARM, read from utils/time_kernel.cpp; only x86 results are published. Single-threaded on both sides (MKL sequential, process pinned to CPU 0); one CPU; padded stride m+16; square float matrices only. -ffast-math applies only to the custom kernel.

notes: README claim and chart verified; the benchmark source compares against MKL with a correctness check and the compiler is named in build_and_run.sh, which is enough for tier A. Metadata confirmed: no license, 1 star, not a fork, last commit 2026-01-10 (active).
